title: FATF Correspondent Banking Guidance excerpt
heading: Section 1. Purpose. This guidance clarifies expectations for correspondent banking relationships under
text:
Section 1. Purpose. This guidance clarifies expectations for correspondent banking relationships under
the FATF Recommendations, particularly Recommendations 10, 13 and 16.

title: FATF Correspondent Banking Guidance excerpt
heading: Section 2. Obligations. Correspondent institutions must understand the respondent bank's AML/CFT
text:
Section 2. Obligations. Correspondent institutions must understand the respondent bank's AML/CFT
controls, customer base, and nested correspondent activity. Payable-through accounts and nested
relationships require enhanced due diligence.

title: FATF Correspondent Banking Guidance excerpt
heading: Section 3. Threshold indicators. Wire transfers routed through nested correspondent chains without
text:
Section 3. Threshold indicators. Wire transfers routed through nested correspondent chains without
transparent originator/beneficiary information should be escalated. Institutions should monitor for
shell-bank indicators and refuse relationships with shell banks.

title: FATF Correspondent Banking Guidance excerpt
heading: Section 4. Transaction monitoring. Unusual patterns in correspondent flows — sudden volume spikes,
text:
Section 4. Transaction monitoring. Unusual patterns in correspondent flows — sudden volume spikes,
high-risk jurisdiction corridors, or repeated just-below-threshold payments — may indicate misuse of
correspondent banking channels.

title: FATF Correspondent Banking Guidance excerpt
heading: Section 5. Reporting. Where suspicion arises regarding correspondent activity, institutions must file a
text:
Section 5. Reporting. Where suspicion arises regarding correspondent activity, institutions must file a
suspicious activity report according to national law and retain decision rationale in the audit trail.

title: FinCEN Advisory Cash Structuring excerpt
heading: Advisory Summary. Structuring occurs when a person conducts or attempts to conduct one or more
text:
Advisory Summary. Structuring occurs when a person conducts or attempts to conduct one or more
transactions in currency, in any amount, at one or more financial institutions, on one or more days, in any
manner, for the purpose of evading currency transaction reporting requirements.

title: FinCEN Advisory Cash Structuring excerpt
heading: Indicator A. Multiple cash deposits or withdrawals just below USD 10,000 within a short window (for
text:
Indicator A. Multiple cash deposits or withdrawals just below USD 10,000 within a short window (for
example, 7 days).

title: FinCEN Advisory Cash Structuring excerpt
heading: Indicator B. Use of multiple accounts or branches to break up large cash amounts.
text: Indicator B. Use of multiple accounts or branches to break up large cash amounts.

title: FinCEN Advisory Cash Structuring excerpt
heading: Indicator C. Customer reluctance to provide identification when a transaction approaches the CTR
text:
Indicator C. Customer reluctance to provide identification when a transaction approaches the CTR
threshold.
Recommended action. Alerts generated for three or more sub-threshold cash transactions by the same
customer within seven days should be investigated and dispositioned with documented rationale.

title: RBI Master Direction KYC AML excerpt
heading: Chapter I. Banks shall undertake customer due diligence and ongoing monitoring proportionate to risk.
text: Chapter I. Banks shall undertake customer due diligence and ongoing monitoring proportionate to risk.

title: RBI Master Direction KYC AML excerpt
heading: Chapter II. Politically exposed persons (PEPs) require senior-management approval and enhanced
text:
Chapter II. Politically exposed persons (PEPs) require senior-management approval and enhanced
ongoing monitoring.

title: RBI Master Direction KYC AML excerpt
heading: Chapter III. Cross-border wire transfers must include complete originator and beneficiary information.
text:
Chapter III. Cross-border wire transfers must include complete originator and beneficiary information.
Incomplete remittance information is an elevated risk factor.

title: RBI Master Direction KYC AML excerpt
heading: Chapter IV. Sanctions screening against applicable lists (including UN and domestic lists) must occur
text:
Chapter IV. Sanctions screening against applicable lists (including UN and domestic lists) must occur
prior to execution where feasible, and hits must be escalated to compliance.

title: RBI Master Direction KYC AML excerpt
heading: Chapter V. Records of alerts, dispositions, and SAR filings shall be retained and made available to
text:
Chapter V. Records of alerts, dispositions, and SAR filings shall be retained and made available to
competent authorities and auditors subject to applicable confidentiality rules.
